intro.text: This entry describes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-123 (DEE123). I do not reliably remember the causal gene or the primary reports on which this entry is based.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders. Seizures usually begin in infancy or early childhood and are often refractory to treatment. Global developmental delay or impairment is present, and both the epileptic activity and the underlying genetic defect are thought to contribute to it. The gene and specific clinical features that define DEE123 are not recalled here.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is a clinically heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Only the abstract was supplied. It does not describe DEE as a clinically heterogeneous group; it reports one proband with a HECW2 variant.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is a genetically heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention DEE or its genetic heterogeneity. It says intellectual disability can have various environmental and genetic causes, which is a different claim.

checks.claim: In developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, seizures usually begin in infancy or early childhood.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract gives no age of seizure onset in DEE generally or in this proband.

checks.claim: In developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, seizures are often refractory to treatment.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention whether seizures were refractory to treatment.

checks.claim: Global developmental delay or impairment is present in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract reports developmental delay in one proband but makes no general statement about DEE.

checks.claim: In developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, both the epileptic activity and the underlying genetic defect are thought to contribute to the developmental impairment.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss how epileptic activity and the genetic defect each contribute to developmental impairment.

paragraphs.text: DEE is genetically heterogeneous, and DEE123 is one of many numbered forms. The specific gene for DEE123 is not stated here because it could not be recalled with confidence.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention DEE or its genetic heterogeneity.

checks.claim: DEE123 is one of many numbered forms of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention DEE123 or the numbering of DEE forms.
